data.text:
Nagdaos ang Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) at ang De La Salle Green Hills ng isang orientation session upang talakayin ang bagong traffic scheme na ipatutupad sa bisinidad ng eskwelahan.

Layunin ng traffic scheme na pagaanin ang traffic congestion sa lugar at sabay na mapanatili ang kaligtasan ng mga estudyante.

Sa programa, ipinaliwanag ng MMDA ang mga pagbabago sa traffic flow, kabilang ang designated lanes, tamang sequencing ng pagpasok at paglabas ng mga sasakyan.  Ang mga bagong patakarang ito ay idinisenyo upang magabayan ang mga magulang at drivers sa araw-araw na hatid-sundo sa mga estudyante.

Binanggit ni MMDA Swift Traffic Action Group (STAG) head Bong Nebrija na sentro ng patakarang ito ang kaligtasan. “Yung safety ang inaalala natin dito,” dagdag niya.  Binigyang-diin niya na ang bagong  traffic scheme ay bahagi ng mas malawak na layunin ng MMDA na gawing mas maayos pa ang paghatid at pagsundo sa mga estudyante sa La Salle Green Hills.

Nabigyan din ng pagkakataon ang mga magulang at mga drivers na magtanong patungkol sa bagong sistemang ipapatupad.

Sa pamamagitan ng kolaborasyong ito, hangad ng MMDA at De La Salle Green Hills na makabuo ng isang mas ligtas, mas disiplinado, at epektibong daloy ng trapiko.

Dumalo rin sa orientation ang iba pang mga opisyal mula sa MMDA at De La Salle Green Hills.

#mmda

DILG 'FULLY PREPARED' FOR NOV. 30 ANTI-CORRUPTION RALLIES

READ: The Department of the Interior and Local Government says it is "fully prepared" to ensure the safe and orderly conduct of the Trillion Peso March at the EDSA People Power Monument in Quezon City on Nov. 30.

The DILG says the permit to carry firearms outside of residence in Metro Manila is also suspended from Nov. 29 to Dec. 1. Only authorities performing official duties in proper uniform are allowed to carry firearms during the said period.

Other progressive groups will stage their anti-corruption protest at the Luneta Park in Manila on Sunday.

SM Prime Holdings chairman Hans Sy recalled what he described as the “hardest moment” of his life — the devastating fire that struck SM Makati.

"I will never forget it because it happened also on my mother's birthday. My father asked me to oversee the rebuilding of the store. When I went to the site during clearing operation, the heat was intense, the air was thick with smoke and ashes, and nothing could be salvaged," Sy said.

"I told myself that no one should ever go through this," he added.

The Dasmariñas Village Association has filed criminal complaints against Rep. Francisco “Kiko” Barzaga and lawyer Trixie Cruz Angeles over the October 12 protest staged near the gates of the exclusive Makati enclave.

In a letter to residents dated November 28, DVA president and chairman José “Coch” Cochingyan III said the association had filed charges with the public prosecutor’s office against Barzaga and Cruz Angeles for allegedly “targeting our community as a ‘class’.”
